title: Labeled ordinary resolution towers and affine descent data
statement:
Fix a totally ordered set $L$. A rational input is a reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme, with no separatedness assumption [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule]. Call such an input embeddable if its structure map factors through a closed immersion into a smooth separated finite-type rational scheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism]. A labeled regular tower is an ordinary tower [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule] with a strictly increasing embedding of its finite set of stages into $L$, coherent nonempty nowhere dense regular centers, and regular last scheme [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-regular-scheme]. A labeled comparison is an ordinary contracted comparison [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule] preserving the retained labels; a labeled cover identification is an uncontracted cartesian comparison [def-per-ordinary-tower-cartesian-map] preserving all labels. Its centers are the full extended ideals [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and its squares use the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product].

A finite affine cover of an input $S$ is a finite affine open cover [def-weil-open-immersion], together with its total disjoint union $U$ as a rational input, the coproduct inclusions and their universal property, and the covering map $U\to S$ over $\mathbf Q$. In particular $U$ is embeddable. Empty covers and empty affine opens are permitted.

A local rule $A$ assigns a labeled regular tower to every embeddable input and a labeled comparison to every smooth rational morphism between such inputs. An affine descent datum consists of $A$, an assignment $R$ of labeled regular towers to all rational inputs, and a labeled cover identification $R(S)|_U\simeq A(U)$ for every finite affine cover. These identifications have the cover-comparison cocycle: for every smooth $v:V\to U$ between two covers of the same $S$, over $S$ and $\mathbf Q$, the local count transported through the two length equalities is the identity on the global level indices, and the two maps from each level of $A(V)$ to the corresponding level of $R(S)$ agree. The identified ideals agree by the center clauses of the cover identifications.

A descended rule for this datum is a smooth-functorial ordinary resolution rule [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule] whose tower on each input is the given $R$ tower, with comparisons preserving its labels. For every smooth $h:T\to S$, every two finite affine covers $U\to S$, $V\to T$, and every smooth induced map $v:V\to U$ over $h$, the comparison restricts to the specified $A(v)$: the counts and survivor embeddings agree under the cover length equalities, and the square of level maps commutes. A stage is deleted if and only if its extended ideal is unit on every lifted affine chart of $V$. The survivor embeddings are identities for identity maps and compose for composite maps. In addition to the count and level-map coherence already required by the ordinary rule, at every retained stage the upper map is the canonical flat blowup base-change map [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map], after identifying the equal center ideals over the lower level; flatness here is [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Explicitly, for the retained lower map $f:B_k\to A_{r(k)}$ and any isomorphism $e:\operatorname{Bl}_{J_k}B_k\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{I_{r(k)}\mathcal O_{B_k}}B_k$ over $B_k$, the upper map, transported by the count equality, is $B_{k+1}\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{J_k}B_k\xrightarrow e\operatorname{Bl}_{I_{r(k)}\mathcal O_{B_k}}B_k\to\operatorname{Bl}_{I_{r(k)}}A_{r(k)}\simeq A_{r(k)+1}$. Thus its affine charts are the canonical tensor base-change maps. Finally, on every empty input, triviality of the local tower implies triviality of the global tower. These are definitions of data and their equations, not assertions that descent is effective.
